title: Patch: the fuzz holds a replayed or restored game to the whole live state, not only to its hash
thread:
**Issue #4058 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4058: Patch: the fuzz holds a replayed or restored game to the whole live state, not only to its hash
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the game server restarts, it saves each live game and loads it back afterwards. A replay rebuilds a game from its moves. The random tester checks both, but only by comparing a fingerprint of the game. That fingerprint deliberately leaves out three things:

- the record of recent moves, which the server uses to answer a repeated message and to show recent events;
- the starting decks a Glitch reset deals again;
- which card created which (the 'Created by' line).

If saving and loading, or replaying, ever got one of those wrong, nothing would notice. After a server restart a player's retried move could get a different answer, a Glitch reset could deal the wrong cards, or a Created card could lose its origin. After this change the tester compares the whole game and names the part that differs. Players never see the check. They see the bugs it stops.

## Why

- **The hash skips three fields by design.** `hash_state` leaves out `applied`, `opening` and `generators` (`crates/engine/src/replay.rs:122-141`): their arrival moved no recorded game's hash.
- **The 1v1 fuzz compares only that hash** in all three places it rebuilds a game:
  - the replay fold, `check_replay` (`crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs:1476-1521`);
  - the JSON round trip, `verify_round_trip` (`fuzz.rs:1553-1566`);
  - the checkpoint continuation (`fuzz.rs:1618-1645`).
- **The three fields matter to players:**
  - `applied` answers a repeated nonce (`crates/engine/src/reduce.rs:684`) and holds every event a view can show (`crates/engine/src/view_for.rs:122`, `:2833`);
  - `opening` is what a Glitch reset deals again (R676, `crates/engine/src/state.rs:1789`);
  - `generators` records a Created card's root (`crates/engine/src/generators.rs`).
- **The server really makes this round trip.** A restart drain stores the engine state as JSON, and the rebuild resumes from it (`crates/server/src/actor/checkpoint.rs:1-9`).
- **Whole-state equality already works.**
  - `GameState` and `DuosState` both derive `PartialEq` (`state.rs:1652`, `crates/engine/src/duos/state.rs:18`).
  - `GameState`'s one skipped field, `fused_scripts`, compares equal by design (`state.rs:1887-1894`).
  - Duos already checks everything: `duos_hash` covers the whole state, nonce logs included (`crates/engine/src/duos/replay.rs:30-38`). The 1v1 games, the ones players play most, get the weaker check.

## Proposal

1. **The replay fold:** in `check_replay`, after the hash and result comparisons, require `replayed.state == run.state`.
2. **The round trip:** give `verify_round_trip` a `PartialEq` bound and require the restored state to equal the original after the hash comparison. Duos goes through it too and gains nothing new, since its hash already covers everything.
3. **The checkpoint:** at the end of the checkpoint continuation, require the continued state to equal the live one.
4. **Name the difference.** On a mismatch, one shared helper names the top-level fields that differ, read from both states as `serde_json::Value`, with the first differing entry inside `applied` or `generators`. The failure then says `replay: generators differs (first at <card id>)` rather than reporting a bare inequality.
5. **Leave `hash_state` alone,** so recorded hashes, the golden fixture and the server's checkpoint checks stay as they are.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`: `check_replay`, `verify_round_trip`, the checkpoint stage, the field-diff helper, and tests beside `a_planted_lossy_round_trip_fails_verification`.
- `crates/tools/src/duos_fuzz.rs`: only as far as the new bound reaches its calls.
- SPEC §9.3 (a log reconstructs any match; the checkpoint) and §10.1 (paused work survives a restore). No rule changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A planted lossy round trip that drops `generators` passes today's hash check but now fails in the checkpoint stage, naming `generators`. A second one that empties `applied` fails the same way, naming `applied`.
- [ ] The existing planted test, which loses one health point, still fails as before.
- [ ] A unit test of the field-diff helper names exactly the top-level keys that differ, and nothing else.
- [ ] These waves pass: `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200`, `cargo jackioh fuzz --handicap --seeds 200` and `cargo jackioh fuzz --duos --seeds 200`. `cargo test -p jackioh-tools` passes, and fmt and clippy are clean.
- [ ] If honest games show a real difference, the pull request does one of two things:
  - fixes it;
  - or, if the difference is intended, writes its ruling (a note in `spec/rulings/`, a test named after it, its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/`) and leaves only that field out of the comparison, saying why.

## Size and risks

- **Size:** small. About 80 lines with tests. Medium difficulty.
- **A difference on day one:** honest games may show a real difference as soon as this lands, for example a fold that fills `opening` or `applied` differently from the live game. That is the finding this check exists for, and the last criterion says how to handle it.
- **Cost:** one struct comparison where a hash is already computed, which is negligible.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43981243374)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

The 1v1 fuzz's three rebuild checks (replay fold, JSON round trip, checkpoint continuation) compare only `hash_state`, which deliberately skips `applied`, `opening` and `generators`. After this change each check also requires full state equality and, on mismatch, one shared helper names the differing top-level fields (with the first differing entry inside `applied` or `generators`), e.g. `replay: generators differs (first at <card id>)`. `hash_state` itself is untouched, so recorded hashes, the golden fixture and the server's checkpoint checks stay as they are. No rule change, so no ruling note.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes there |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` | change | New `state_diff` helper beside `verify_round_trip`; full-state equality in `check_replay`, `verify_round_trip` (new `PartialEq` bound) and `check_serial_restart_with`; new tests in `fuzz_serial_restart` plus a helper unit test |
| `crates/tools/src/duos_fuzz.rs` | change | Mirror equality asserts in `check_duos_run` and `check_duos_serial_restart_with` (the new bound already holds: `DuosState` derives `PartialEq`); no new helper, no new tests needed |

Do not touch: anything under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/` or `bot/`; `crates/engine/` (especially `replay.rs`'s `hash_state`); `spec/` (no ruling, no `spec/pending/` paragraph: no semantics decision); `apps/web`, `e2e`. Governing spec: §9.3 (`spec/09-architecture.md`, log reconstructs any match plus the checkpoint) and §10.1 (`spec/10-engine-guide.md`, paused work survives a restore). Cited rulings (unchanged): R676 (`opening`), R1956001 (`generators`), R768 (replay refusal on hash mismatch).

## Steps

1. In `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`, next to `verify_round_trip` (~line 1553), add `pub(crate) fn state_diff(live: &Value, other: &Value) -> Vec<String>`. Both args are `serde_json::to_value` of the two states. Walk the union of top-level keys in document order (left's order, then right-only extras); for each key with unequal values push one entry: `{field} differs`, or `{field} differs (first at {at})` when `field` is `applied` or `generators` and a first entry is found. `first at` for `generators` (both objects): the first key in left order, then right order, whose value differs or is missing on one side — that key is the card id. For `applied` (both arrays): the first index with unequal elements; detail is that element's `nonce` string when it is an object carrying one, else `#{index}`; when one array is a strict prefix of the other, detail is `#{min_len}`. Any other shape mismatch yields no detail. Empty vec means equal.
2. In the same file, give `verify_round_trip` a `PartialEq` bound (`S: Serialize + for<'de> Deserialize<'de> + PartialEq`) and, after the existing hash comparison, serialize both states to `Value` and run `state_diff`. Keep the current hash-mismatch message byte-for-byte, appending ` ({diff joined with ", "})` when the diff is non-empty, so the existing planted test's `contains("the round trip changed the state")` still holds. When the hashes are equal but `restored != *state`, return `Err` with `the round trip changed the state: {diff}` — this is the arm that catches a dropped `generators` or emptied `applied`, which the hash cannot see.
3. In `check_replay` (~line 1476), after the hash and `result` comparisons, add `if replayed.state != run.state` failing in `FailureStage::Replay` with `replay: {diff} differs — folding (seed, log) did not reproduce the match (§9.3)` for one entry (`replay: generators differs (first at <card id>)`), entries joined with `, ` for several. `Value`s come from `serde_json::to_value(&run.state)` and `&replayed.state`; both infallible here (both serialize in `hash_state` already).
4. In `check_serial_restart_with` (~line 1590), after the continuation's hash and `result` comparisons and before the time-bound check, add `if state != *live` failing in `FailureStage::Checkpoint` with `checkpoint: {diff} differs — the restored game diverged (§9.3)`, same joining rule as step 3.
5. In `crates/tools/src/duos_fuzz.rs`, in `check_duos_run` after the hash and ending checks, add `if replayed.state != run.state` returning `Err` with `the fold reached a different state: {diff}` using `crate::fuzz::state_diff` on the two `DuosState` values. In `check_duos_serial_restart_with` after its hash and ending checks, add the same comparison against `live`, prefixed `checkpoint: `. Expect no behavior change: `duos_hash` already covers the whole state, so these asserts are consistency guards.
6. Add the tests listed below in `fuzz.rs` (helper unit test in a new small `mod state_diff_tests`; the rest in `mod fuzz_serial_restart`, reusing its `seed_one`, `run`, `lossy` and `seed_one_checkpoint` helpers). For tamper tests, mutate a clone (clear `generators`, or `applied.clear()`), never the live run.

## Tests

- `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`, `state_diff_tests::state_diff_names_exactly_the_fields_that_differ`: hand-built `json!` objects differing in `generators` (one changed root plus one missing key) and `turn`, asserting the returned vec is exactly `["generators differs (first at <the changed card id>)", "turn differs"]`; plus an equal-objects case returning empty. Proves keys are exact and nothing else is named.
- `fuzz_serial_restart::a_lossy_round_trip_that_drops_generators_fails_naming_generators`: `lossy` = `round_trip` then `restored.generators.clear()`; assert `verify_round_trip` errs and the message names `generators`. Also assert `hash_state` of both is equal, proving today's check is blind to it.
- `fuzz_serial_restart::a_lossy_round_trip_that_empties_applied_fails_naming_applied`: same with `restored.applied.clear()`, message names `applied`, hashes equal.
- `fuzz_serial_restart::a_replay_that_loses_generators_fails_naming_generators` and `..._empties_applied_...`: `seed_one()` run with `run.state.generators.clear()` / `run.state.applied.clear()`, then `check_replay` fails in `FailureStage::Replay` naming the field.
- `fuzz_serial_restart::a_checkpoint_continuation_that_loses_generators_fails_naming_generators` and `..._loses_applied_...`: `seed_one_checkpoint(&run, &run.log, &tampered_live)` fails in `FailureStage::Checkpoint` naming the field (exercises step 4's end-of-continuation equality).
- Existing `a_planted_lossy_round_trip_fails_verification` and `a_restored_game_that_misses_the_live_hash_fails_in_the_checkpoint_stage` stay as they are and must still pass unmodified.
- Commands: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools fuzz_serial_restart`, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools state_diff`, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools duos_checkpoint_stage`, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools` (full crate), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check`. Builder also runs the three acceptance waves: `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200`, `cargo jackioh fuzz --handicap --seeds 200`, `cargo jackioh fuzz --duos --seeds 200`.

## Done when

- [ ] A planted lossy round trip dropping `generators` passes the hash comparison yet fails in the checkpoint stage naming `generators`; ditto for emptied `applied`.
- [ ] The existing planted health-point test still fails exactly as before (message keeps its prefix).
- [ ] The helper unit test names exactly the differing top-level keys and nothing else.
- [ ] `check_replay`, `verify_round_trip` and the checkpoint continuation all require full equality in 1v1; duos mirrors them; `hash_state` is byte-identical to before.
- [ ] The three 200-seed waves, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools`, fmt, clippy and `spec check` are clean.
- [ ] If an honest wave shows a real difference: either fix the divergence, or — only if the difference is intended behavior — write its ruling (note in `spec/rulings/`, test named after it, §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/4058.md`) and exclude just that field with the reason in a comment; never silently drop a field.

## Risks

- A day-one honest difference (e.g. a fold filling `applied` or `opening` differently from the live game) fails seeds that pass today. Checked the likely sources and they look safe: repeated nonces return a clone without appending to `applied` (`reduce.rs`), the `NONCE_HISTORY` trim is order-deterministic so fold and live agree, `opening` comes from the same `create_options`/`fold_args`, `generators` is deterministic, and `fused_scripts` compares equal by design across a JSON trip. If a wave still goes red, the last Done item governs — fix it, don't weaken the check.
- `serde_json::to_value` key order is struct declaration order on both sides, so "document order" and "first at" are deterministic across threads and runs; no sorting, no hash-ordered iteration.
- No hidden-information or client risk: all new code lives in `crates/tools` (the fuzzer), never in the engine, server or views.

## Open questions

None. The only judgment call — honest difference versus intended behavior — is settled by the last Done item, which needs no person: fix it, or rule it and exclude one field.
```
